title: Major Depressive Disorder & Generalized Anxiety
guideline: APA Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients with Major Depressive Disorder / CANMAT Guidelines

clinical_targets.goal: ≥ 50% reduction in depressive / anxiety symptoms on validated rating scales (PHQ-9, GAD-7)
PHQ-9 < 5; return to full functional baseline and social occupational role
Continue therapeutic dose for at least 6–12 months after remission to prevent relapse

steps.title: First-Line Monotherapy: SSRIs & SNRIs
steps.rationale: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) and Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors (SNRIs) have the best balance of efficacy and tolerability.

drug_classes.dosing: Escitalopram start 10 mg daily (titrate to 20 mg); Sertraline start 50 mg daily (titrate to 100–200 mg).
drug_classes.pearls: Full therapeutic onset takes 4–6 weeks. Warn patient of transient mild nausea and anxiety during first 1–2 weeks. Never discontinue abruptly.

steps.title: Second-Line / Switching or Augmentation
steps.rationale: If inadequate response after 6–8 weeks at therapeutic dose, switch to another SSRI, switch to an SNRI or Atypical agent, or augment.

drug_classes.role: Alternative with zero sexual dysfunction and no weight gain.
drug_classes.dosing: Bupropion XL 150–300 mg once daily morning; Mirtazapine 15–45 mg once daily at bedtime.
drug_classes.pearls: Bupropion is activating (contraindicated in seizure disorder or eating disorders). Mirtazapine is sedating and promotes appetite/weight gain.

special_populations.elderly: Start at half the standard adult starting dose (e.g. Escitalopram 5 mg, Sertraline 25 mg). Check for SIADH / hyponatremia. Max Escitalopram 10 mg in elderly due to QTc prolongation risk.
special_populations.pregnancy_lactation: Sertraline is commonly preferred due to lower concentration in breast milk.

monitoring: Evaluate for treatment-emergent suicidality, particularly in patients aged < 25 years during the first 1–2 months. Monitor QTc on ECG if Escitalopram or Citalopram at higher doses.
